title: Pasting Spring Festival Couplets
synopsis: Spring Festival couplets are one of the oldest traditions to celebrate the Chinese New Year.

fullText.simplified:
贴春联

    虽然很多人觉得汉字很难，但在外面看到汉字还是会试着读一下。如果看到的汉字是认识的，可能又会觉得汉字很有意思。春节的时候，商场和每家的家门口都会贴一些红色的纸，纸上写着一些汉字。这些红色的纸是庆祝春节的春联。春联上的汉字很漂亮，有很多种字体。如果你对春联和汉字的字体不太了解，你可能看不懂这些汉字。
    春联在中国已经有两千多年历史了，最初的春联上没有汉字，只是红纸。两千多年前的中国人认为鬼害怕红色的东西，所以就在门上贴红色的纸。当鬼看到门上的红纸，会觉得害怕，就不敢进来了。三百多年前，一个皇帝希望人们有文化，能多认识一些字，就在这些红纸上写了新年愿望。人们觉得非常有意思，就跟着把自己的新年愿望也写在了门上的红纸上。一年年过去，慢慢地，春联就变成了今天的样子。
    贴春联是中国人的一个习惯，每年春节都会贴。春联上的汉字表达的是人们对新年的希望和祝福。
    当然，中国很大，每个地方的习惯会有些不一样。听说有个地方，如果家里有人去世，他们会三年不贴春联，因为他们觉得这样去世的亲人就能进门和家人一起过春节了。
fullText.traditional:
貼春聯

    雖然很多人覺得漢字很難，但在外面看到漢字還是會試著讀一下。如果看到的漢字是認識的，可能又會覺得漢字很有意思。春節的時候，商場和每家的家門口都會貼一些紅色的紙，紙上寫著一些漢字。這些紅色的紙是慶祝春節的春聯。春聯上的漢字很漂亮，有很多種字體。如果你對春聯和漢字的字體不太了解，你可能看不懂這些漢字。
    春聯在中國已經有兩千多年歷史了，最初的春聯上沒有漢字，只是紅紙。兩千多年前的中國人認為鬼害怕紅色的東西，所以就在門上貼紅色的紙。當鬼看到門上的紅紙，會覺得害怕，就不敢進來了。三百多年前，一個皇帝希望人們有文化，能多認識一些字，就在這些紅紙上寫了新年願望。人們覺得非常有意思，就跟著把自己的新年願望也寫在了門上的紅紙上。一年年過去，慢慢地，春聯就變成了今天的樣子。
    貼春聯是中國人的一個習慣，每年春節都會貼。春聯上的漢字表達的是人們對新年的希望和祝福。
    當然，中國很大，每個地方的習慣會有些不一樣。聽說有個地方，如果家裡有人去世，他們會三年不貼春聯，因為他們覺得這樣去世的親人就能進門和家人一起過春節了。

sentence_translations: Pasting Spring Festival Couplets
Although many people find Chinese characters very difficult, if they see Chinese characters outside, they will still try and read them.
If the Chinese characters are ones that they recognize, they might feel that Chinese characters are very interesting.
During the Spring Festival, red pieces of paper are pasted in shopping malls and at the front door of every house.
There are Chinese characters written on these red papers.
These red pieces of paper are Spring Festival couplets to celebrate the Spring Festival.
The Chinese characters on the Spring Festival couplets are very beautiful, with all sorts of calligraphic styles.
If you aren’t very familiar with Spring Festival couplets and their calligraphic styles, ..
.. you might not be able to understand the Chinese characters.
Spring Festival couplets already have more than 2,000 years of history in China.
The first Spring Festival couplets didn’t have any Chinese characters. They were just red pieces of paper.
Chinese people more than 2,000 years ago believed that ghosts were scared of red things, ..
.. so they pasted red pieces of paper on their doors.
When the ghosts saw the red pieces of paper on the doors, they would feel scared and not dare to enter.
Around 300 years ago, an emperor hoped that people would be literate and learn some more characters, ..
.. so wrote some New Year wishes on the red pieces of paper.
People thought this was very interesting and also started writing New Year wishes on the pieces of red paper on their doors.
The years passed by, and gradually, Spring Festival couplets became what they are today.
Pasting Spring Festival couplets is a custom of Chinese people every year during the Spring Festival.
The Chinese characters on the Spring Festival couplets are people’s hopes and blessings for the New Year.
Of course, China is huge, so the customs in place will be a little different.
Apparently, there is a place where if someone in the family has passed away, they won’t paste Spring Festival couplets for three years ..
.. because they think that this way, the family member who passed away will be able to come in to celebrate Spring Festival with the family.
